title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 12 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Corinthians chapter 12 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 12 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Corinthians Chapter 12.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 12, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord
A thorn in the flesh was given to me
He was caught up into paradise
I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago
questions.correctAnswer: I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:1 states the author will come to visions and revelations of the Lord, which is the earliest event mentioned in the chapter.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians, how long ago did Paul know a man in Christ?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:2 says, 'I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago.'

questions.question: Where was the man caught up to, according to 2 Corinthians 12?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:2 mentions that the man was caught up to the third heaven.

questions.question: What does Paul say about whether the man was in the body or out of the body?
options: He cannot tell whether in the body or out of the body
He was definitely out of the body
He was definitely in the body
He was neither in nor out of the body
questions.correctAnswer: He cannot tell whether in the body or out of the body
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:3 states, 'whether in the body, or out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth.'

questions.question: Into what place was the man caught up, where he heard unspeakable words?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:4 says he was caught up into paradise and heard unspeakable words.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 12, what kind of words did the man hear in paradise?
options: Unspeakable words which it is not lawful for a man to utter
questions.correctAnswer: Unspeakable words which it is not lawful for a man to utter
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:4 describes the words as unspeakable and not lawful for a man to utter.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 12, Paul says he will glory in what?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:5 says, 'yet of myself I will not glory, but in mine infirmities.'

questions.question: Why does Paul say he will not be a fool to glory?
options: Because he will say the truth
questions.correctAnswer: Because he will say the truth
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:6 states, 'For though I would desire to glory, I shall not be a fool; for I will say the truth.'

questions.question: What is the reason Paul forbears glorying in himself?
options: Lest any man should think of him above what they see or hear
questions.correctAnswer: Lest any man should think of him above what they see or hear
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:6 explains Paul forbears glorying lest any man should think of him above that which they see or hear.

questions.question: What was given to Paul to keep him from being exalted above measure?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:7 states, 'there was given to me a thorn in the flesh... lest I should be exalted above measure.'

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 12, who is the messenger that buffets Paul?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:7 describes the thorn in the flesh as 'the messenger of Satan to buffet me.'

questions.question: Paul says he knew a man caught up to the third heaven whether in the body or out of the body; God knows. True or False?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:2 states Paul knew a man caught up to the third heaven, but whether in or out of the body he cannot tell; God knows.

questions.question: Paul says he will glory in his infirmities rather than glory in himself. True or False?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:5 states Paul will glory in his infirmities and not in himself.

questions.question: Paul says the thorn in the flesh was given to him to make him stronger and more powerful.
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:7 says the thorn was given to buffet Paul and to keep him from being exalted above measure, not to make him stronger or more powerful.

questions.question: Paul explicitly states in 2 Corinthians 12 that he heard the unspeakable words in the third heaven.
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:4 states the man was caught up into paradise and heard unspeakable words, but the third heaven was mentioned in verse 2 without specifying the hearing of words there.

medium.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 12 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Corinthians Chapter 12 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How many times did Paul besought the Lord regarding his affliction?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is found in 2 Corinthians 12:8 where Paul states he besought the Lord thrice.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 12:9 promise will happen if someone embraces their weaknesses?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:9 states that God's strength is made perfect in weakness, implying that embracing weaknesses leads to strength.

questions.question: What does Paul say he takes pleasure in for Christ's sake?
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 12:10, Paul asserts that he takes pleasure in infirmities, which reflects his understanding of strength in weakness.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 12:11, why does Paul feel compelled to glory?
options: Because of the lack of commendation from the Corinthians
questions.correctAnswer: Because of the lack of commendation from the Corinthians
questions.explanation: Paul mentions in 2 Corinthians 12:11 that he has become a fool in glorying because the Corinthians have compelled him to do so due to their lack of commendation.

questions.question: What signs were wrought among the Corinthians according to 2 Corinthians 12:12?
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 12:12, Paul states that the signs of an apostle were demonstrated among the Corinthians through signs, wonders, and mighty deeds.

questions.question: What does Paul express about his relationship with the Corinthians in 2 Corinthians 12:13?
options: He has not been burdensome to them
They are inferior to other churches
questions.correctAnswer: He has not been burdensome to them
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 12:13, Paul acknowledges that he himself was not burdensome to them, highlighting his selflessness.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 12:14, what does Paul seek from the Corinthians?
questions.explanation: Paul expresses in 2 Corinthians 12:14 that he seeks not theirs but them, indicating his desire for their well-being rather than material gain.

questions.question: What does Paul mean by 'when I am weak, then am I strong' in 2 Corinthians 12:10?
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 12:10, Paul's statement reflects his understanding that his weaknesses allow Christ's power to rest upon him, leading to true strength.

questions.question: What does Paul say about boasting in 2 Corinthians 12:5?
options: He will boast in his strengths
He will not boast at all
He will boast in his infirmities
He will boast in his revelations
questions.correctAnswer: He will boast in his infirmities
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 12:5, Paul states that he will glory in his infirmities rather than in his own strengths or revelations.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 12:7, what was given to Paul to prevent him from being exalted above measure?
questions.explanation: Paul mentions in 2 Corinthians 12:7 that a thorn in the flesh was given to him to prevent him from being exalted above measure.

questions.question: What does Paul mean when he says he is 'nothing' in relation to the chiefest apostles in 2 Corinthians 12:11?
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 12:11, Paul's statement reflects his humility, acknowledging his position compared to the chiefest apostles.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 12:9, how does Paul describe God's grace?
questions.explanation: Paul states in 2 Corinthians 12:9 that God's grace is sufficient for him, emphasizing its adequacy in times of need.

questions.question: Is it true that Paul was seeking material gain from the Corinthians?
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 12:14, Paul states that he seeks not theirs but them, indicating he is not after material gain.

questions.question: Is it true that Paul boasted about his weaknesses?
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 12:5, Paul mentions that he will glory in his infirmities, indicating he does boast about his weaknesses.

questions.question: Is it true that Paul felt he was inferior to other apostles?
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 12:11, Paul states that he is not behind the very chiefest apostles, indicating he does not see himself as inferior.

hard.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 12 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Corinthians Chapter 12.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 12:15, Paul expresses his willingness to spend and be spent for the Corinthians. What contrasting emotional outcome does he mention?
options: The more abundantly I love you, the less I be loved
The more I teach you, the less you understand
The more I serve you, the less you appreciate
The more I visit you, the less you welcome me
questions.correctAnswer: The more abundantly I love you, the less I be loved
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:15 states, 'though the more abundantly I love you, the less I be loved,' showing Paul's lament about love's reciprocity.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 12:16, how does Paul describe his method of dealing with the Corinthians despite not burdening them?
options: Being crafty, I caught you with guile
Being straightforward, I taught you plainly
Being gentle, I guided you with love
Being forceful, I compelled you to obey
questions.correctAnswer: Being crafty, I caught you with guile
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:16 says, 'nevertheless, being crafty, I caught you with guile,' indicating Paul's strategic approach while avoiding burdening them.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 12:17, Paul asks if he made any gain from the Corinthians through those he sent. What is his implied answer?
options: No, he did not make a gain
He was uncertain about the gain
questions.correctAnswer: No, he did not make a gain
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:17 questions, 'Did I make a gain of you by any of them whom I sent unto you?' with the implied answer being no, emphasizing Paul's selflessness.

questions.question: Who did Paul desire to accompany Titus when he sent him to the Corinthians, as mentioned in 2 Corinthians 12:18?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:18 states, 'I desired Titus, and with him I sent a brother,' identifying the companion sent along with Titus.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 12:19, Paul says they speak before God in Christ. What is the primary purpose he gives for their actions?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:19 clarifies, 'we do all things, dearly beloved, for your edifying,' showing Paul's sincere care for the Corinthians' spiritual growth.

questions.question: What is one of the specific fears Paul expresses about his coming to the Corinthians in 2 Corinthians 12:20?
options: Lest there be debates, envyings, wraths, strifes, backbitings, whisperings, swellings, tumults
Lest he will be rejected by the elders
Lest the city be destroyed before he arrives
Lest the people will forget his teachings
questions.correctAnswer: Lest there be debates, envyings, wraths, strifes, backbitings, whisperings, swellings, tumults
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:20 explicitly lists Paul's fears of divisive behaviors among the Corinthians upon his arrival.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'ἐκκόπτω' (ekkoptō) in 2 Corinthians 12:16 mean?
options: To cut off or catch with guile
questions.correctAnswer: To cut off or catch with guile
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'ἐκκόπτω' in 2 Corinthians 12:16 relates to the idea of 'catching' or 'cutting off' craftily or with guile, consistent with Paul's description.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in 2 Corinthians 12:15 where Paul contrasts his love and the love he receives?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:15 uses antithesis by contrasting 'the more abundantly I love you' with 'the less I be loved' to highlight the disparity in affection.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of Paul's 'thorn in the flesh' as a messenger from Satan buffeting him (2 Corinthians 12:7)?
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:6 describes serpents sent among the people as a form of divine punishment, paralleling the 'messenger of Satan' buffeting Paul in 2 Corinthians 12:7.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage fulfills the theme of strength in weakness expressed in 2 Corinthians 12:9?
questions.explanation: Philippians 4:13 ('I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me') echoes the theme in 2 Corinthians 12:9 of divine strength perfected in human weakness.

questions.question: What verse immediately precedes Paul's statement in 2 Corinthians 12:15 about gladly spending and being spent for the Corinthians?
options: 2 Corinthians 12:14 - Behold, the third time I am ready to come to you; and I will not be burdensome to you
2 Corinthians 12:13 - For what is it wherein ye were inferior to other churches
2 Corinthians 12:16 - But be it so, I did not burden you
2 Corinthians 12:12 - Truly the signs of an apostle were wrought among you
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Corinthians 12:14 - Behold, the third time I am ready to come to you; and I will not be burdensome to you
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:14 directly precedes verse 15 and sets the context for Paul's readiness to visit without being burdensome.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the typology of Paul's 'thorn in the flesh' in 2 Corinthians 12:7?
options: A symbol of human weakness allowing divine power to be displayed
A sign of divine punishment for sin
A metaphor for persecution by authorities
questions.correctAnswer: A symbol of human weakness allowing divine power to be displayed
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:7-9 shows the thorn as a means by which Paul's weakness highlights the power of Christ, a common typological understanding.

questions.question: How does Paul use chiasmus in 2 Corinthians 12:18 to emphasize unity with Titus and his companions?
options: By paralleling 'walked we not in the same spirit?' with 'walked we not in the same steps?'
By listing multiple apostles and their works
By repeating the phrase 'with him I sent a brother'
questions.correctAnswer: By paralleling 'walked we not in the same spirit?' with 'walked we not in the same steps?'
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:18 employs chiasmus through the parallel questions highlighting shared spirit and steps, emphasizing close unity.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Corinthians 12:21, Paul fears he will find many unrepentant sinners in Corinth when he comes again.
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:21 explicitly states Paul's fear that he will bewail many who have sinned and not repented upon his return.

questions.question: True or False: In 2 Corinthians 12:9, Paul states that his strength comes from his own perseverance rather than God's grace.
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:9 clearly states, 'My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness,' attributing strength to God's grace, not Paul's perseverance.

theological.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 12 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Corinthians Chapter 12 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 12:5 teach about human weakness and divine glory?
options: God's power is perfected in human infirmities
Human weakness disqualifies one from divine glory
Infirmities separate man from God's grace
questions.correctAnswer: God's power is perfected in human infirmities
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:5 teaches that Paul chooses to glory not in himself but in his infirmities, implying that God's power is manifested and perfected through human weakness.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 12:7 teach about the purpose of spiritual trials in the life of a believer?
options: Trials prevent believers from becoming prideful due to revelations
Trials indicate God's displeasure with the believer
Trials are irrelevant to spiritual growth
questions.correctAnswer: Trials prevent believers from becoming prideful due to revelations
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 12:7, Paul explains that the 'thorn in the flesh' was given to prevent him from being exalted above measure through the abundance of revelations, indicating that trials serve to humble the believer.

questions.question: What doctrine about apostolic authority is taught in 2 Corinthians 12:12?
options: True apostles are confirmed by signs, wonders, and mighty deeds
Apostolic authority is solely based on teaching accuracy
Apostolic authority comes from human institutions
Miracles are unrelated to apostolic legitimacy
questions.correctAnswer: True apostles are confirmed by signs, wonders, and mighty deeds
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:12 states that the signs of an apostle were performed with patience, signs, wonders, and mighty deeds among the Corinthians, confirming apostolic authority.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Corinthians 12:9 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:9 records God’s declaration, 'My grace is sufficient for thee,' explicitly demonstrating the divine attribute of grace.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified in 2 Corinthians 12:21 regarding God's dealings with unrepentant sin?
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 12:21, Paul expresses fear that God will humble him among those who have sinned and not repented, highlighting God's holiness and intolerance of sin.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 12:1–4 connect with the broader biblical theme of divine revelation and heavenly visions?
options: It exemplifies the continuation of God revealing Himself through visions as seen in Old Testament prophets
It contradicts Old Testament teachings about visions
It denies the possibility of divine visions in the New Testament era
It focuses solely on human imagination
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies the continuation of God revealing Himself through visions as seen in Old Testament prophets
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:1–4 recounts Paul’s experience of visions and revelations, aligning with the biblical pattern of God revealing truth through visions as with prophets in the Old Testament (e.g., Ezekiel, Daniel).

questions.question: In what way does 2 Corinthians 12:10 reflect the Pauline theme of strength being made perfect in weakness found elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It echoes the teaching that human weakness is the context for divine power to be displayed, as seen also in Romans 8
It teaches that weakness is a sign of spiritual failure
It contradicts the idea of grace empowering weakness
It emphasizes self-sufficiency over divine strength
questions.correctAnswer: It echoes the teaching that human weakness is the context for divine power to be displayed, as seen also in Romans 8
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:10’s statement 'when I am weak, then am I strong' reflects the Pauline theology that God's power is perfected in human weakness, a theme consistent with Romans 8's teaching on life in the Spirit.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Corinthians 12:8 and 12:9 teach about prayer and God's response to suffering?
options: God may not remove suffering but provides sufficient grace to endure it
God always removes suffering immediately upon prayer
Prayer is ineffective in altering suffering
Suffering is punishment that cannot be alleviated
questions.correctAnswer: God may not remove suffering but provides sufficient grace to endure it
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 12:8 Paul prays thrice for removal of his thorn, but 12:9 reveals God’s response emphasizing grace sufficiency and strength perfected in weakness, indicating God’s sustaining grace over removal.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Corinthians 12:14 and 12:15 teach about Christian self-sacrifice and familial responsibility?
options: Parents should provide sacrificially for their children, reflecting Christ’s love
Children are obligated to financially support their parents primarily
Self-sacrifice is unnecessary in Christian leadership
questions.correctAnswer: Parents should provide sacrificially for their children, reflecting Christ’s love
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:14 teaches that parents ought to lay up for their children, and 12:15 shows Paul’s willingness to spend and be spent for the Corinthians, illustrating sacrificial parental love modeled on Christ.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Corinthians 12:19 and 12:20 teach about apostolic concern and church discipline?
options: Apostles act out of love for church edification and fear of sin’s destructive effects
Apostolic ministry ignores church behavior and discipline
Church disputes are irrelevant to apostolic work
Apostles seek personal glory through church conflict
questions.correctAnswer: Apostles act out of love for church edification and fear of sin’s destructive effects
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 12:19, Paul asserts he acts for the believers' edifying, and in 12:20, he fears finding discord and sin among them, showing an apostolic burden for holiness and unity.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Paul's 'thorn in the flesh' was removed because he prayed thrice. What does 2 Corinthians 12:7-9 actually teach about this matter?
options: The thorn was not removed; God’s grace was given instead to empower Paul in weakness
The thorn was a physical illness immediately healed
Paul stopped praying after the third request
The thorn was removed but Paul continued to suffer in other ways
questions.correctAnswer: The thorn was not removed; God’s grace was given instead to empower Paul in weakness
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:7-9 shows that despite Paul’s thrice prayer, God said, 'My grace is sufficient for thee,' implying the thorn remained but grace empowered him.

questions.question: What doctrine about apostolic humility is taught in 2 Corinthians 12:6 and 12:11?
options: True apostles refrain from boasting except in their weaknesses and service
Apostles should boast of their achievements to gain respect
Apostolic authority depends on public recognition
Humility is irrelevant to apostolic ministry
questions.correctAnswer: True apostles refrain from boasting except in their weaknesses and service
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 12:6 and 12:11, Paul avoids foolish boasting, preferring to boast in infirmities and expresses that he should have been commended for his service, emphasizing apostolic humility.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly reflected in 2 Corinthians 12:2–4 regarding Paul's visionary experience?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:2–4 recounts Paul caught up to the third heaven and paradise, experiences that demonstrate God's transcendence beyond earthly realms.

questions.question: What narrative arc is fulfilled by Paul's discussion of his 'thorn in the flesh' in 2 Corinthians 12:7-10 in relation to Christ’s sufficiency?
options: The theme of divine strength perfected in human weakness culminating in Christ’s sustaining grace
The theme of divine abandonment in suffering
The theme of human merit earning salvation
The theme of punishment without hope of restoration
questions.correctAnswer: The theme of divine strength perfected in human weakness culminating in Christ’s sustaining grace
questions.explanation: Paul’s thorn and God’s response in 12:7-10 illustrate the biblical narrative of God’s strength made perfect in weakness, emphasizing Christ’s sufficiency in human frailty.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Corinthians 12:16 and 12:17 teach about apostolic integrity and method in ministry?
options: Apostles may use shrewdness but do not exploit believers for gain
Deceptive gain is acceptable in ministry
Apostolic ministry is driven by personal profit
questions.correctAnswer: Apostles may use shrewdness but do not exploit believers for gain
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 12:16 Paul admits to craftiness to catch the Corinthians but denies making gain from them in 12:17, teaching integrity despite strategic methods.
